title: Release notes
summary: A public Releases page lists what shipped and when across web, iOS, the kiosk, and the Mac app, going back to the first build.
details: The page opens on the last eight weeks, with earlier history one click away.
Filter by app (Web, iOS, Kiosk, Mac) or by new features, improvements, and fixes.
Weekly fix roundups fold into one line you can expand.
Follow along with the RSS feed.
Every future update adds its own entry here.

title: Staff gear picks
summary: Staff can choose their 2027-28 apparel and equipment in the app within their allowance, then review and submit, while organizers see everyone's picks in one place.
details: A catalog with an allowance bar shows what you've picked and what's left as you go.
Review lets you change size, quantity, and color inline, and sizes default from your profile.
A short How it works intro appears on your first visit and can be reopened from the header.
Your picks are kept if a save or reload fails, and Show all gear clears filters when nothing matches.
Organizers see results and can export them as a CSV.

title: Item cleanup wizard
summary: A guided wizard walks staff through items one at a time to fill gaps in inventory records, so labels, serials, and accessories are accurate before they're needed.
details: Confirm or fill in each item's QR label and serial number.
Attach cages, plates, and grips to the camera they belong to.

title: Damage report review
summary: Damage reports filed at the kiosk now land on the dashboard, where staff can see the photo and send the item to maintenance in one step.
details: Each report opens a review panel with the photo, the reporter's notes, and a link to the item.
Reports can cover numbered batteries and counted supplies, not just individually tracked gear.

title: Kiosk stops auto-selecting kits
summary: Kiosk checkout no longer picks a suggested kit for you; you choose a kit only when you want one.
details: The suggested kit is still highlighted in the kit picker so it's easy to find.
Choosing a kit uses it as your checklist while you scan gear.

title: YouTube metadata tool
summary: Admins can connect the program's YouTube channel and keep video titles, descriptions, and playlists consistent from inside the app.
details: A YouTube page connects or disconnects the team channel.
A review queue lists the last 30 days of videos with suggested titles and descriptions.
Editors save a draft per video, then review and publish titles, descriptions, and playlists.
Naming rules guide the suggestions so uploads follow one house style.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Kit, kiosk, and calendar fixes from the week after the kiosk redesign.
details: Football travel kits can share cameras with game-day kits, and kit pages find batteries again.
Kiosk no longer offers to change items on a pending pickup where that isn't possible.
Today and Tomorrow sections on a kiosk left running overnight now roll over at midnight.
Cleaned up many small kiosk layout, title, and wording issues.

title: Label print cart
summary: Staff can collect item labels in a print cart, review them, and export ready-to-print files, instead of printing labels one at a time.
details: Add labels to the cart from across the app and review them before printing.
Export a separate file for each label printer template.

title: iOS sign-in redesign
summary: The iPhone app's launch and sign-in screens get a cleaner dark design and calmer handling of offline and expired sessions, along with better date pickers.
details: An offline launch offers Try again, and an expired session shows a calm notice instead of an error.
Today, Tomorrow, and Now labels roll over at midnight if the app stays open overnight.
Subscribed shift calendars use full sport names, with promotion details moved to the event notes.

title: Workforce and student hiring
summary: Admins get a Workforce area that shows the whole staff and student picture and runs student hiring cycles from application to account invite.
details: An overview shows staff and students by area, with class standing, graduation, start terms, and sport assignments.
A Planning tab projects student headcount per area for coming years, including graduating, hired, and pipeline.
Hiring tracks applicants through Applied, Reviewed, Round 1, Hire, and Passed, with resumes, interview links, and notes.
Import applicants and roster history from spreadsheets, and upload many resumes matched by file name.
Marking someone Hire creates a prefilled student invitation that links to their account once they sign up.
Applicant personal details are removed automatically after the retention period for a closed cycle.

title: Calmer iPhone Home and Schedule
summary: iPhone Home and Schedule move to a flatter, calmer style that puts what's next first.
details: Home uses flat cards, number-first stats, and one Next Up list grouped into Overdue, Today, and Later.
A Schedule card on Home lists upcoming team events you aren't working, with near times like in 45 min.
Schedule, Trade Board, and event detail open at the current or next event.
Schedule remembers your filters, flags overlapping shifts, and lists trades and open slots together, soonest first.

title: Kiosk staff ID and pickup editing
summary: A round of kiosk follow-ups from live use on the iPad: staff actions now need a staff ID card, pickups can be edited, and battery problems can be reported.
details: Staff scan their staff ID card to change someone else's due time or transfer their checkout.
Change a pickup's title, event, and due time right at the kiosk.
Report a problem now covers numbered batteries and counted supplies, so a return can still finish.
Someone checking out for an event they aren't staffed on can request a crew spot for admin review.
Open an event from Events today to see its crew, their gear, and who still needs gear.
Checkout preselects your next shift, and booking sheets group gear by category with photos and tags.

title: Kiosk redesign
summary: The kiosk is rebuilt across home, person hub, checkout, pickup, and return, with clearer steps and new ways to hand off, undo, and report gear without finding a staff member.
details: Home groups overdue, due today, pickups, and game-day crews, with photos and the week's reservations when quiet.
Hand all or part of a checkout to anyone on the roster, or nudge an overdue holder once a day.
Undo a mistaken scan, swap a unit for the same model in one scan, and get a receipt after checkout.
Report gear as damaged, with an optional photo, or missing during a return; staff are notified.
Scans show when gear is next needed, play distinct sounds by result, and extensions show the latest possible return.
Larger system type, flat surfaces, a color per section, time presets, and a month calendar for return dates.

title: Football travel support
summary: Road trips are easier to staff and return from: travel gear can be returned by anyone at the kiosk, and default travelers are added in one step.
details: Anyone signed in at the kiosk can return items from another person's checkout as travel gear comes back.
Add defaults on an away game's Travel card puts every default traveler for that sport on the trip.
Default travelers can be turned off again, are listed first, and only people who can travel are offered.

title: Notification controls
summary: Notifications are easier to control and more dependable, with per-type levels, quiet hours, shift reminders, and alerts that group instead of piling up.
details: iOS: Set each notification type to Off, Silent, or Standard, set quiet hours, and pause until a chosen time.
You get a reminder two hours before a published shift with the event, area, and call time.
Alerts group by checkout or event, newer updates replace older ones, and wording says what to do next.
iOS: Lock-screen actions include Mark as Read, Remind Me in 1 Hour, and Approve or Decline for admins.
The app icon badge matches your unread count, and iOS Settings links straight to notification settings.
Delivery is tracked end to end, retries no longer send duplicates, and every type follows your settings.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Schedule safeguards, Mac app polish, and reservation fixes.
details: A reservation transferred to someone else can be picked up normally.
Crew edits from an outdated screen can no longer overwrite a newer schedule draft.
Shift calendar links are better protected, and the app asks before resetting your link.
Mac: Booking details support Esc, Return, a Copy Ref button, and a right-click menu, and overdue rows read Was due.

title: Redesigned iOS Schedule
summary: The iPhone Schedule becomes one continuous list with a week strip, and the Trade Board and shift feed get a round of reliability fixes.
details: A swipeable week strip jumps through the list and expands into a month grid.
Quick filter chips and toolbar toggles for My Shifts and Sport, with your own work highlighted.
Opens instantly from your last view; pull down for earlier weeks, and every role can browse past events.
Open slots show how many student claims are waiting and link to the Trade Board.
Trade Board drops trades on cancelled events, keeps call times on approval, and reports results correctly.
The shift calendar feed shows only published crews, and its link sheet adds Share Link.

title: QR Studio
summary: A free public tool on the site makes branded, scan-checked QR codes, so anyone on the team can make a reliable code without third-party generators.
details: Make codes for links, Wi-Fi, email, phone, text messages, and contacts.
Each code is checked to scan correctly before you download it.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Notification links, guide reading, and Items fixes, plus Mac and badge polish.
details: Every notification, widget, quick action, and link now opens the matching page, including licenses, badges, and the Trade Board.
iOS no longer crashes when one person has two shifts on an event.
Guide table of contents stays pinned and highlights the section you're reading.
Items address bar matches the current filters, and the default Items sort loads faster.
Mac booking alerts update in place, stay silent unless sound is on, and open the booking.
Badge celebrations link to your shelf, and the iOS badge gallery matches the web layout.

title: Guides in search and Resources handbook
summary: Guides are easier to find and read: they now show up in app-wide search, and Resources opens like a handbook.
details: Quick search and the Search page match guides by title, category, author, summary, and content.
Resources opens with a featured guide, guides grouped by type, jump chips, and a tools strip.
How-to guides support copyable paths and commands, screenshots between steps, and before/after images.
The guide editor adds a Callout menu and a Video button, and iOS renders guides like the web.

title: Web navigation, settings, and profiles
summary: The web app's sidebar, Settings, and profiles are reorganized so common destinations are easier to find.
details: The sidebar groups daily work, Team, Library, and Operations, and notifications move to a bell in the top bar.
Settings opens on a searchable directory, with Booking and Schedule settings grouped separately.
Profiles lead with role, title or year, and a Scoreboard link, with Info split into Contact, Work, and Assignments.
The team Scoreboard leads with the official record, and its filters are saved in a shareable link.

title: Schedule toolbar and activity
summary: The web Schedule is simpler to filter and browse, shows what changed recently, and gives staff more scheduling tools.
details: The toolbar has View, My Shifts, a searchable Sport filter, a Filters panel, and Clear.
A pinned activity strip shows recent assignments and calendar changes, with old and new values.
The list starts around today and loads older and newer events as you scroll.
Add event starts as a home game today and fills the title from sport and opponent.
Auto assign adds Scope and Review steps, and staff can add slots, publish now, and hold overlapping shifts.

title: iOS 27 look and New Reservation
summary: The iPhone app picks up the iOS 27 look and a cleaner way to build reservations.
details: Refined Liquid Glass styling with bars that recede while scrolling, while still supporting iOS 26.
Pickup and return share one row with a 15-minute time menu, and Review appears once gear is chosen.
Gear search sits in the navigation bar, rows swipe to add or remove, and unavailable gear is marked.
Review names who holds conflicting gear and uses a stepper for counted supplies.

title: Redesigned event page
summary: The event page is reorganized around crew, travel, and activity, with crew management and claim review happening right on each row.
details: Separate crew, travel, and activity cards, with crew fill in the header and a timeline of calendar changes.
Filled rows offer Replace and Unassign, and open rows offer Assign and Remove.
Pending claims and trades show as avatars on crew rows, with Approve and Decline for admins.
One form creates and edits events, and hand-added events can be hidden or deleted.
Ended events let staff record people who worked without a slot, without notifying anyone.

title: Game-day kits
summary: Kits bundle a camera package so anyone can reserve or check out a full game-day setup in one step on the web, iPhone, or kiosk.
details: Choosing a kit adds its cameras, lenses, and batteries to a reservation or checkout for review.
Football kits can be assigned game-day jobs, and pickers suggest the kit from your last game.
Kiosk checkout can start from a kit, showing its remaining items as a scan checklist.
Pickup lists a kit's actual items, empty kits are hidden, and each camera belongs to one kit per sport.

title: Re-reserve a past booking
summary: Start next week's reservation from a completed booking, with the person, pickup location, notes, and gear already filled in.
details: Works from completed checkouts and past reservations on the web and iPhone.
The copy is shifted to a new event of your choosing.

title: Flexible kiosk pickups
summary: Kiosk pickups now match what actually leaves the room: add or remove items, swap units, and pick up leftovers later on the same checkout.
details: Scan an extra item to add it to the reservation, or remove items you aren't taking.
Scanning a different unit than the one reserved can swap it in.
Gear picked up later joins the same open checkout, and the reservation shows only what's still waiting.
Blocked items explain who has them, maintenance, or a shortage in a popup that stays until dismissed.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Steadier forms, filters, and lists across web and iOS, plus Mac sign-in and battery return fixes.
details: Mac app no longer loses its sign-in, and sign-out sticks after relaunch.
Event coverage counts only confirmed crew, and blocked releases name the conflicting event and time.
Reservation Rules and Checkout Policies warn about unsaved changes and recover drafts after a refresh.
Filters and search boxes handle duplicate names, Enter, and international keyboards more reliably.
iOS: Errors stay pinned above the form with your entries kept, and lists stay visible while refreshing.
Kiosk battery returns record where and by whom they were scanned.

title: Publish a schedule now
summary: Admins can send pending crew changes immediately instead of waiting for the release timer, useful for last-minute changes.
details: Publishing early runs the same checks as a timed release.
Workers on future events get the usual change notifications.
Changes still release on the ten-minute timer unless an admin publishes them sooner.

title: Transfer items between checkouts
summary: Staff can move a checked-out item to another person, adding it to their checkout or a new one, while keeping the item's history intact.
details: The item's original scan and photo records stay with it after the move.
Return reminders follow the item to the receiving checkout.
A checkout left with no gear closes as a canceled transfer.

title: Merge duplicate checkouts
summary: Staff can combine duplicate checkouts for the same event into one, choosing the due-back time when they differ.
details: Staff can select up to 25 matching checkouts and merge them into the oldest one.
Custody, numbered batteries, and scan history all carry over to the merged checkout.
Checkouts for different people, events, or locations, or with partial returns, can't be merged.
When duplicates came from different reservations, staff choose which reservation link to keep.

title: Clearer blocked items at the kiosk
summary: Reserved or unavailable items are stopped before they reach the kiosk cart, with a clear explanation and next steps.
details: Blocked items are rejected with a sound and never enter the cart.
The kiosk says who has the item reserved or checked out and when it is due back.
Remove the item, change the return time, or keep scanning without losing the cart.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Shift claim scoping, signature, battery, and Schedule fixes.
details: Students claim open shifts and trades only in their primary area, and the Trade Board lists teammates' trade posts separately.
Away and neutral-site events no longer show students a call time.
Signatures with many strokes, such as printed names, now save.
Kiosk battery scans count correctly across kiosks, and pickup lists batteries as a count.
Schedule list reliably opens at today and warns when data may be out of date.
Staff can remove a player from a signature roster, and admins can turn a reservation into a checkout.

title: Shared travel cases
summary: Team travel cases can be reserved and checked out as shared gear that any operator can handle, without counting against one person.
details: Any signed-in operator can pick up or return a shared case at the kiosk, and each scan is recorded.
Shared cases count as team work and stay out of anyone's My Gear and Accountability record.
Reminders go to the responsible staff and admins instead of a single borrower.

title: Combine overlapping events
summary: Staff can merge same-sport events at one venue into a single Schedule row and crew, so overlapping games don't need duplicate staffing.
details: The Schedule suggests pairs that can be combined.
Preview the combined crew before saving, and undo it later.
Combined events show as one row on the web and iPhone, naming the shared crew.

title: Extend up to the next booking
summary: An active checkout can be extended right up to the start of the next booking for that gear, and the app shows when the gear is needed next.
details: True overlaps and stock shortages still block an extension.
New reservations still keep the standard turnaround time between bookings.
On iPhone, booking details show the limit before you open Extend.

title: Partial kiosk pickups
summary: Scan only some of a reservation's gear at the kiosk; the rest stays reserved for a later pickup.
details: Each pickup starts a checkout for only the gear you scanned.
The reservation completes once its last item is picked up.
A reservation's gear list can't be edited after pickup has started.

title: Group badge awards
summary: Admins can search people, select a group, and award a badge to everyone at once from the Badges page, with a summary of what was awarded.
details: Admins can select every visible search result, clear the selection, and review names before confirming.
One group award can reach up to 200 people.
People who already hold the badge are skipped instead of receiving it twice.
Recipients get the usual in-app notification for their new badge.

title: Add items in bulk
summary: Adding new gear is faster: create a whole shipment of serialized items at once, or start a new unit from an existing one.
details: Create up to 25 items in one step with shared details and per-row tags and serials, including pasted lists.
Add another like this copies product details and suggests the next asset tag and a fresh QR code.
The Add item form puts required fields first and jumps to any field that needs fixing.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Kiosk home, time picking, and account fixes, plus many small reliability improvements.
details: Kiosk home lists every active checkout, overdue first, with clearer due times.
Event, call, and return times now use 15-minute steps and round forward.
Deleting your account removes your personal profile and sign-in data while keeping gear history.
Bookings, Items, and Schedule keep your filters and place when you go back.
Password managers save and fill the right account on every password screen.
Accessibility improves across iOS and the kiosk, and the Mac menu bar icon can be hidden.

title: iPhone widgets and quick actions
summary: Your shifts and gear are reachable without opening the app, through Home Screen widgets, icon quick actions, Spotlight, and lock-screen notification actions.
details: Next Shift and My Gear widgets stay current and open the exact event or booking.
Long-press the app icon for Scan, My Gear, Schedule, and New Reservation with live counts.
Find your bookings from Spotlight.
Snooze a gear reminder, view the booking or shift, or acknowledge an announcement from the lock screen.

title: Android browser push
summary: Students on Android can turn on push notifications for the web app from Settings and send themselves a test.
details: Tapping a notification opens the matching page in the web app.
Browser pushes follow your existing notification preferences.
Signing out turns off push for that browser, and iPhone notifications are unchanged.

title: iPhone Bookings filters and swipes
summary: Bookings on iPhone is quicker to work through, with saved filters, sorting, and swipe actions.
details: Status scopes like Overdue, Due Today, and Reserved, plus sorting, and your choice is remembered.
Swipe a booking to Edit, Transfer, Extend, or Cancel.
Students see the team list, with a Mine toggle for just their own.

title: Brand asset library
summary: Resources gains a Brand assets tab that keeps logos, fonts, templates, and the brand guide in one place, organized like a file drive.
details: Folders with a side rail, breadcrumbs, Recent and Starred views, and sortable columns.
Previews for images, PDFs, and fonts, plus favorites.
Drag and drop to upload anywhere in a folder, with version history when files are replaced.

title: Claim shifts from Schedule
summary: Students can request open shifts and manage their trade posts right where they browse, and admins review every claim.
details: Request, see Awaiting approval, or withdraw on Schedule rows and the event crew list.
See whether a trade post is open or claimed, and remove it.
Only admins approve or decline claims and trades, and they receive the review alerts.

title: Gear conflict checks
summary: Reservation pickers and kiosk scans check each item as you go, so conflicts surface before you build a booking around unavailable gear.
details: Pickers block conflicting items and say when an item is needed next or back.
Real blockers are separated from tight-turnaround advisories.
Kiosk scans show any conflict or shortage for that item and hold checkout if availability can't be confirmed.

title: Preview the app as another role
summary: Admins can see exactly what other people see, in a read-only view, without changing their own access.
details: On the web, preview as Staff, Student, or a partner collaborator.
On iPhone, switch into a Student view from Settings, marked by a subtle orange screen edge.

title: Link bookings to five events
summary: Reservations and checkouts can now be linked to as many as five scheduled events, on the web and iPhone.
details: The earliest linked event is treated as the booking's primary event.
Reservations keep all their linked events when they become checkouts.
The event picker hides past events but keeps existing past links visible.
Kiosk checkouts still link to a single event or purpose.

title: Season Scoreboard
summary: Profiles and a new team Scoreboard show season records and events worked, so students and staff can see the games they've covered at a glance.
details: Profiles show a win-loss-tie record, recent form, highlights, and games grouped by month.
Breakdowns by sport, opponent, site, and venue, with exhibitions and scrimmages left out of official records.
A separate total counts every completed event you worked, including non-game work.
The team Scoreboard is open to everyone and stacks sport, venue, opponent, and site filters.
Results sync from the athletics calendar, and admins can add collaborators to events for team totals.
Available on web and iPhone, with collaborators seeing team totals without others' details.

title: Simpler sign-in for invitees
summary: Signing in is simpler: invited people start from the normal sign-in page, and saved passkeys appear as soon as you tap the email field.
details: New invitees enter their email on the regular sign-in screen and choose a password there.
Saved passkeys show as suggestions in the email field on web and in the iPhone keyboard bar.
Remember me covers passkey sign-ins, and Account and Security shows whether each passkey is synced.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Date, kiosk, and iOS fixes, plus bulk invitations and signature updates.
details: All-day shifts and license expiry dates no longer appear a day early.
iOS: Guide photos, tables, and captions render correctly, and Home shows every overdue item.
Fixed several kiosk layout issues, including wrapped names and the activation keypad being covered.
Live Production shifts can be added from iPhone, and notification times show in Central time.
Staff can invite people in bulk by uploading an email and role CSV.
Signature roster downloads come as PNG or SVG, and an Administration roster is added.

title: Shift claims need approval
summary: Open-slot pickups and Trade Board claims are held for review again, and the original owner keeps the shift until a claim is approved.
details: Several students can request the same open slot, and staff choose who gets it.
Approving one request automatically declines the others for that slot.
Staff approve or decline both open-slot requests and Trade Board claims.

title: Fifty automatic badges
summary: The automatic badge catalog grows to fifty, and working events now earns credits toward stats and badges.
details: New badges recognize work across sports and crews, night and doubleheader shifts, gear variety, and trades.
Automatic awards leave an inbox notification so you see them later.
The iOS badge page matches the web, and the kiosk celebrates earned badges with rarity colors.

title: Class schedules and days away
summary: Availability leads with weekly class times and makes it easy to block off trips and other time away.
details: Weekly classes can be tied to class-term dates.
One-off entries can cover a date range or a full day.

title: Mac app alerts and launch at login
summary: A menu bar app keeps open bookings, pickups, and kiosk health in view on the Mac.
details: Optional booking alerts and a count in the menu bar.
Launch at login, and it stays signed in across restarts and network hiccups.

title: Kiosk operator hub
summary: The kiosk hub shows your bookings beside your upcoming shifts, and scanning gets clearer feedback.
details: Start a checkout linked to one of your shifts in one tap.
Pickup and return show the same large scan confirmation as checkout, with a running count.
Add Items on an active checkout can use the camera, and the roster fits on one screen.

title: Shared software logins
summary: Staff can keep shared software logins in the app next to the Photo Mechanic license pool, visible only to the people who need them.
details: Reveal, copy, archive, or restore each shared login.
Choose whether each login is shown to staff, students, collaborators, or a mix.
Licenses opens on Photo Mechanic with your activation code first, and shared logins one tab over.

title: Crew editor in Schedule
summary: Staff can open the full crew editor straight from a Schedule row and see what's changed recently.
details: The row menu sets up Home, Away, or empty crews and opens the same editor as event detail.
The editor hides people already assigned, offers retries, and confirms before reverting.
Synced calendar and assignment changes from the last day open as a list with event links.
Event detail shows when pending crew changes will be sent and who will be notified.

title: Rebuilt iPhone event detail
summary: Event detail on iPhone now leads with one main action, such as assigning the next open slot or claiming a shift.
details: Coverage is visible to everyone, and cancelled events are clearly marked.
The student call time shows once, and open slots are tappable rows.
Crew row menus are grouped, and events can be shared or copied.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: A kiosk crash, calendar display, and name formatting were fixed this week.
details: Kiosk: Fixed a crash after scanning a numbered battery during pickup or return.
Subscribed all-day shifts show as a single day in Apple Calendar.
Team abbreviations stay in capitals on bookings, the dashboard, and the kiosk.
Trade Board keeps showing open shifts or trades if one fails to load, and explains blocked trades.
iOS: Sign-in asks for your email first, then your password.
The web app's browser and home-screen icons use the Block W.

title: Signature capture
summary: Staff can capture player, coach, and staff signatures with Apple Pencil on iPad and download them for graphics.
details: Download signatures as transparent PNG or vector SVG, or a whole roster as a ZIP.
Import rosters for more sports, plus a separate Creative staff roster and one-off signers.
Recapturing keeps earlier versions, and several iPads can capture at once without overwriting each other.
Progress counts student-athletes first, completed rows turn green, and Quick Look previews signatures.
Other devices show a disabled Capture on iPad button.

title: Mac menu bar app
summary: A new Mac menu bar app keeps your gear, bookings, and notifications a click away.
details: Booking alerts lead with the booking title, with status, requester, and time below.
The menu shows open bookings, pickups, and kiosk health.
Booking alerts and a menu bar count are optional, and the app can launch at login.

title: Reports rebuilt, now on iPhone
summary: Reports focus on gear use and compare against the prior period, and staff can view them on iPhone.
details: iOS: Staff open Reports from Browse to see utilization, checkout activity, status breakdown, most-used gear, and idle counts.
Choose a 30- or 90-day window.
Reports say when part of the data failed to load instead of showing zeros.

title: Staged overdue reminders
summary: Overdue checkouts now follow a five-stage reminder schedule, so the right people hear about late gear at the right time.
details: Alerts route to the responder for the checkout's location.
Admins are brought in if a checkout stays overdue.

title: New badges and kiosk celebrations
summary: Ten new badges and milestones arrive, and earning one now comes with a celebration.
details: New badges reward things like checkout variety, away assignments, and early call times.
Kiosk: Badges earned during checkout, pickup, or return appear on the success screen.
After a transfer, the original borrower keeps checkout credit and the new holder earns return credit.
People who had met a goal without receiving its badge now have it.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Schedule edits, checkout handling, and several web and iPhone details were fixed this week.
details: Removed shifts stay removed after calendar sync, and their workers are notified.
Canceled reservations no longer block unassigning, editing, or publishing the Schedule.
Checked-out gear closes only through a kiosk return or an admin exception.
Scanning now lives in the iOS app and kiosk; the web scan page is retired.
iOS: Booking details list every linked event and show only actions you can take.
Collaborators allowed to reserve gear see New reservation on Home again.

title: Timed schedule release
summary: Crew edits now release to workers automatically after a ten-minute quiet period, so quick changes don't trigger a flood of notifications.
details: A countdown shows when assignees will be notified, with Revert available until then.
Only workers whose shifts changed are notified.
Workers whose shift didn't change keep their acknowledgement after a republish.

title: Whole-schedule drafts
summary: Staff now build the schedule in a private draft on web or iPhone and publish when it's ready.
details: Publishing lists every blocker at once before anything is saved.
A stale draft can be refreshed against the live schedule instead of being discarded.
An Unpublished drafts chip shows events held by a draft.
iOS: Adding shifts, assigning or replacing people, and changing call windows stay private until published.

title: Event reservations join the crew
summary: Reserving gear for an event now adds you to that event's crew, keeping the schedule and gear in sync.
details: Canceling or transferring the reservation updates the crew assignment.
You're placed on the reservation's primary event, in an open slot or a new one.
The usual schedule conflict and approved time-off checks still apply.
Events without a crew setup and unpublished schedule drafts are left unchanged.

title: Crew call times and slot replacement
summary: Staff have new tools to manage who works an event and when they report.
details: Replace the person on a filled slot, with checks for trades, linked gear, conflicts, and time off.
Set one call time for a whole crew, then add individual exceptions.
Changing a sport's default call time updates upcoming shifts but leaves hand-set times alone.
Call times show only on student shifts; neutral-site games use the away crew template.
Admins set staffing defaults for non-game events, and new events use them automatically.

title: Register and reset passwords in the app
summary: Invited users can now create an account and request a password reset without leaving the iPhone app.
details: Sign-in screens suggest using your campus email when an Athletics address is typed.
Only invited email addresses can register, just like on the web.
Registering signs you straight into the app once your account is created.

title: Kiosks across all locations
summary: Any staffed kiosk now works for everyone, showing the full roster and every checkout and reservation.
details: Returned gear is moved to the kiosk where it was returned.
Roster and Wiscard lookup include every active team member, regardless of saved location.

title: Sign in with a passkey
summary: You can now sign in with a passkey on the web and iPhone instead of typing a password.
details: Add, view, and remove passkeys from Security settings.
Password sign-in still works.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Session handling, permissions, badges, and several booking edits were fixed this week.
details: Hardened sign-in sessions on iPhone and kiosk; signing out clears notifications and cached data.
Deactivating a user signs them out everywhere and stops their reminders.
Collaborator controls match exactly what each account is allowed to do.
Quick extend works again, and back-to-back edits no longer report a conflict.
Trade Board refreshes when someone else claims a shift first.
Fixed several badge award rules, including damage-free credit for late returns.

title: Staff announcements
summary: Staff can send an announcement to an event crew, specific people, or groups, and it appears as a banner in the app.
details: The banner stays at the top of the iPhone Home screen until the recipient taps Got it.
Each announcement also arrives as a push notification and in the notification inbox.
Senders can see who received, read, and acknowledged each announcement.

title: In-app tips on iPhone
summary: One-time tips point out new features like New Reservation, Trade Board, Shift Calendar, My Availability, and continuous scanning.
details: Each tip appears once and goes away after you use the feature.
Shift Calendar and My Availability tips appear only after a few visits to Schedule.
A tip on the reservation draft card explains how to resume a minimized reservation.

title: Reservation drafts
summary: Unfinished reservations on iPhone can be minimized or saved as drafts and finished later on iPhone or the web.
details: Minimize a reservation in progress to a card and keep browsing.
Retrying an interrupted submit returns the original reservation instead of creating a duplicate.
Dashboard totals and active bookings don't count drafts.

title: Photos when adding items
summary: New items and item families can include a photo from search, a pasted link, or an upload before saving.
details: A failed photo can be retried without re-creating the item.
Photo search for a new item family starts from the family name.
Adding stock to an existing quantity item keeps its current photo.

title: Rebuilt kiosk checkout
summary: Kiosk checkout is now two steps, details then scan, and the home screen leads with what's due today.
details: The scanner shows clearly when it is disconnected.
The roster has clear loading, error, and retry states.

title: Pending Pickup
summary: Reservations now become Pending Pickup at their start time and appear on the dashboard, so staff can see who still needs to collect gear.
details: Pending Pickup shows in orange, and missed pickups say when they were due.
Uncollected reservations are released automatically after the no-show window.
Reservation Rules explain pickup and no-show timing.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Kiosk warnings, draft names, notification colors, and date labels were fixed and polished this week.
details: Kiosk: Battery checkouts no longer show false tight-turnaround warnings.
Kiosk: A checkout closes on its own when the last item is scanned back.
People added in an unpublished draft keep their name and photo after a refresh.
Booking detail shows the requester, timing, location, gear count, and linked event in one summary.
Dashboard rows read Today, Tomorrow, or Yesterday for nearby dates.
iOS: Notification colors match their meaning, and screens do less work while drawing.

title: Accountability report
summary: Admins can see late returns ranked across the academic year to follow up where gear keeps coming back late.
details: Late extensions are included.
Export to CSV, with the option to exclude test data.

title: People directory for collaborators
summary: Admins can let partner collaborators find active teammates by name and see a limited work profile without contact details.
details: Collaborator sign-up adds a phone step, which can be skipped and added later.
Organization badges keep their original casing.

title: Rebalanced badges
summary: The badge catalog is rebalanced with new milestones, unique art, and rarity that reflects how many people actually hold each badge.
details: New checkout, on-time, scan, and damage-free milestones.
Shift badges return, and streaks are shown.
Every badge on iOS shows its own icon.

title: Profiles and a personal iPhone Home
summary: Profiles share one rebuilt layout, and iPhone Home now centers on your own day.
details: Profiles show gear out, upcoming reservations, title and class year, a badge shelf, and Email and Call buttons.
iOS: Home counts, pending pickups, and the Bookings badge reflect only your own work.
iOS: Bookings is one time-ordered list, and overdue rows say how late they are.

title: Draft crew changes
summary: Staff edit crews in a private draft and publish when ready, with a review of exactly who will be notified.
details: The crew editor shows only areas in use, one row per slot, and inline call times.
Sport is a top-level Schedule filter, and the picker ranks people by fit, availability, and workload.
Crew setup uses the sport's template for games and asks which defaults to use for other events.
Sport crew defaults save explicitly and update only untouched upcoming slots.

title: Overdue nudges by push
summary: When staff nudge someone about an overdue checkout, the borrower now also gets a push notification that opens the checkout.
details: The push follows the borrower's overdue checkout notification setting.
The in-app reminder still arrives when push is off or unavailable.
Nudging doesn't change the checkout's status or due time.

title: Redesigned iPhone Schedule
summary: Schedule on iPhone is rebuilt so your shifts stand out and staff can staff events faster.
details: List and calendar share one event card, with your shifts marked.
Event detail puts your assignment, linked gear, and Claim controls right under the event name.
Staff assign from a ranked Best Fits list that explains availability, overlap, and workload.
My Availability uses a tappable weekly canvas, and the Trade Board leads with claimable shifts.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Reservation limits, sign-in, profile updates, and many smaller details were fixed and polished this week.
details: Reservations with many numbered units stay pickable, and reservation limits apply reliably.
iOS: Sign-in and sign-out are more reliable, and a wrong password gets a clear message.
Profile edits show up in the Users roster immediately.
Changing a shift's time saves conflicts and history together.
Controls across Items, Bookings, Schedule, and Resources are larger and keyboard accessible.
iOS: Notification settings are simpler and include Send Test Notification.

title: Rebuilt New Reservation on iPhone
summary: New Reservation on iPhone now walks through Details, Gear, and Review steps, starting from an event or a manual booking.
details: Pickup and return are set separately in 15-minute steps; event bookings default around the event.
Browse Cameras, Lenses, Batteries, and Other, with battery suggestions and counts like 42/46 available.
If gear becomes unavailable on submit, you return to Gear with your picks kept.
Finished reservations open right away, and the event shows a Gear reserved row.

title: Redesigned iPhone bookings and items
summary: Booking and item screens on iPhone lead with who has the gear and when it's due.
details: Booking Detail opens with the holder, title, and live timing, plus a pinned Extend button.
Bookings use friendly due dates like Due Monday at 8:30 AM and a Mine/All toggle.
Long-press a booking to edit, transfer, extend, or cancel it.
Item Detail shows the photo, tag, current holder, and upcoming and previous bookings.

title: Collaborator accounts
summary: Admins can give partner organizations accounts with permissions they control, so outside collaborators can use the app safely.
details: Admins create affiliations, choose what they can do, suspend or reactivate them, and preview who a change affects.
Collaborators see only the Home modules, tabs, and actions their access allows.
Eligible collaborators appear on the kiosk roster without needing a Wiscard.
iOS: Collaborators get a read-only Published Schedule with crew previews and follow or mute.

title: Welcome setup for new accounts
summary: New accounts sign up with just name, email, and password, then complete a welcome setup that asks only what their role needs.
details: Returning users missing details get a short guided setup they can snooze for a day.
Profile photos can be cropped, zoomed, and repositioned before upload.
Profiles hold separate personal and work phones, and student profiles show anticipated graduation.

title: Scan-first kiosk
summary: Scanning on the kiosk home screen now recognizes what you scanned and opens the right flow.
details: A scan can identify a person, available gear, a checkout, or a reservation.
Upcoming reservations can be picked up before their start time.
Counted items can be confirmed at pickup without scanning each one.
The scanner reconnects on its own and shows Scanner ready or Scanner reconnecting.

title: Booking quick view refresh
summary: The booking quick view leads with timing and urgency, and common edits happen inline.
details: Edit title, times, and notes directly in the sheet.
Transfer, relink events, and cancel live under More actions.
Dashboard rows lead with the person's avatar, with timing easier to scan.

title: Multiple products in an item family
summary: An item family can now hold units from several product models while still appearing as one row and one reservation line.
details: Each numbered unit can be assigned to its specific product.
Staff can replace an item family's QR code while keeping counts and history.
Item family pages lead with active stock, and retired units no longer count toward totals.

title: Operations page
summary: Fix Today checks, data cleanup, and battery tools now live together on one Operations page.
details: Fix Today checks are for admins, while Keep data clean checks are open to staff.
The page shows only checks that need work and folds clean ones into a summary.
A battery summary card links straight to Battery Ops.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Stock counts, all-day events, trades, and push delivery got important fixes this week.
details: Battery and other bulk stock counts stay accurate however gear is edited or returned.
Kiosk: A reservation pickup rolls back cleanly if a battery is taken mid-pickup.
Trade Board posts can no longer double-book a shift, and cancelled games leave subscribed calendars.
All-day events show on the right day without made-up call times or false conflicts.
Gear shown as available in the picker is no longer rejected on submit.
iOS: Push notifications deliver reliably again.

title: iPhone Settings and app icons
summary: The iPhone app gets a dedicated Settings page laid out like iOS Settings, with account controls and app icon choices.
details: Account & Security includes a password-confirmed Delete Account option.
Settings links to the privacy policy and support.
Choose an alternate app icon from five designs.
If push setup fails, Notifications explains the problem and offers Retry.

title: iPhone accessibility and faster launch
summary: The iPhone app works better with larger text, VoiceOver, and Reduce Motion, and opens faster for returning users.
details: Home, Search, sign-in, notifications, reservations, Schedule, Guides, and Licenses support larger text and better labels.
Returning users go straight into the app, with a branded splash on cold launch.
On iPad, the Browse sidebar can be reordered.

title: Cleaner web navigation and inbox
summary: Web navigation, notifications, and list pages are reorganized to lead with what needs attention.
details: The sidebar highlights one active page, and Users appears for every role.
The notification inbox has All and Unread filters and opens the right page for each notification.
Bookings show status badges and gear thumbnails, and Items, Kits, and Licenses get status summary rails.
Settings pages use the full width and are renamed by what they do.

title: Transfer bookings and relink events
summary: Active bookings can now move to another person or change their linked events without touching the gear or pickup.
details: Staff can transfer any active booking; students can transfer their own.
Link, change, or clear the events on an active booking from its detail page.

title: Scan to edit kiosk checkouts
summary: Opening an active checkout at the kiosk arms the scanner, so adding gear is as simple as scanning it.
details: Each scan adds an item immediately, and every item has its own Remove button with confirmation.
Rapid scans all land in the cart, and checkout waits for pending scans.
Booking history names exactly which item was added or returned and at which kiosk.

title: Kiosk portrait and split view
summary: The kiosk app now runs in any iPad orientation and window size.
details: Checkout, pickup, return, and the hub stack neatly in portrait or narrow windows.
Header and completion buttons use the latest iPadOS glass styling.
The home screen updates after each task and has a manual refresh button.

title: Redesigned activity timelines
summary: Item, booking, user, and audit histories are easier to read at a glance.
details: Clear event icons, before-and-after values, and links to related checkouts and reservations.
Booking activity notes when a return came in late and by how much.

title: Event types and calendar sync
summary: Events now use four clear types, and calendar sync is more dependable.
details: Creating or editing an event asks for Home, Away, Neutral, or Non-game; games require a sport and opponent.
Calendar sync handles slow feeds and time zones and flags events that disappeared for review.

title: Resources reader overhaul
summary: Resources gets a new guide reader, instant search, and a cleaner hub, so staff and students find how-tos faster.
details: Press Cmd+K to search guides by title, category, author, or content.
Guide authors can insert Note, Tip, and Warning callouts and video embeds from the toolbar.
The reader shows related guides in the same section with previous and next links.
The hub has one search field, a Sport assignments directory, and faster loading.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: False conflicts, all-day event times, kiosk typing, and other issues were fixed this week.
details: Editing a checkout keeps its numbered batteries instead of turning them into a plain count.
Editing only a booking's title or notes no longer triggers false availability conflicts.
iOS: All-day events show as date-only instead of midnight times, including with VoiceOver.
Kiosk: The keyboard stays open while typing, and battery counts show on active checkouts.
The notification bell count and license alert times work again.
Hardened kiosk activation and signing out of other devices.

title: Siri and Shortcuts
summary: Ask Siri about your gear and shifts without opening the app, and build Shortcuts around common tasks.
details: Ask what gear you have out or when your next shift is.
Shortcuts can open a booking, scan, view My Gear, see today's schedule, or start a reservation.

title: Live Activity updates
summary: The return countdown now keeps itself current, so it reflects your checkout even if you never open the app.
details: Live Activities can start on their own when a return is due.
Extending or editing a checkout updates the countdown, and cancelling removes it.
A green Returned confirmation appears once the gear is back.

title: Search-first iPhone reservations
summary: Creating a reservation on iPhone is rebuilt around search: find gear, tap to add, and keep going.
details: A pinned cart handles quantities, with popular items shown first.
Scan tags continuously to add gear.
Start from an event to fill in the reservation title and time.

title: Instant shift claims and staff trade posting
summary: Open student shifts and Trade Board claims now take effect immediately, and staff can put a student's shift up for trade.
details: Claiming assigns you right away instead of waiting for approval, including from iOS event detail.
Staff can post or remove a student's shift on the Trade Board, and the student is notified.
iOS: Crew rows show when a shift is posted, with trade actions in the long-press menu.

title: Unified iPhone Bookings
summary: iPhone Bookings now shows checkouts and reservations in one fresher list, and booking details can be edited in place.
details: One searchable list with Reserved, Checked Out, and Overdue labels.
Mine, All, and Attention views are one tap away, and stale rows no longer appear.
An Edit Details sheet changes a booking's title, pickup and return times, notes, and pickup location.
Rapid taps on Save, Extend, or Cancel no longer send duplicate requests.

title: Badge trophy shelf
summary: Badges now display as a trophy shelf of compact medallions on web and iOS, with a summary of your progress.
details: Badges are grouped into collections with earned counts.
iOS: The Users directory and profiles get a new card design with role colors and clearer badge sections.

title: Kiosk visual refresh
summary: Every kiosk screen gets a consistent new look and smoother motion, and checkout setup is easier to fill in.
details: Checkout setup has side-by-side event and return sections, matching web reservations.
Return time uses a calendar and time picker, with a pinned Start Scanning button.
The hub, scan screens, sleep mode, and success screen share the new design.

title: Public About pages
summary: A public set of About pages explains what the app does, how it is built, and how it is secured, alongside a privacy policy.
details: The pages describe real workflows and the platform in plain language, using fictional sample data in product screens.
iPhone Settings links to the privacy policy and support.

title: Browse tab, Guides, and Licenses on iPhone
summary: The iPhone app gets a Browse tab and native Guides and Licenses screens, so common resources no longer open a web view.
details: Browse groups Items, Guides, Licenses, and the Users directory, which is now open to every role.
Search is its own tab at the end of the tab bar, with the QR scanner in its toolbar.
Guides have search, filters, sorting, and a built-in reader.
Licenses let you see the pool, claim or return a seat, and copy your active code.

title: Availability and Trade Board upgrades
summary: Availability is now fully editable on iPhone and shows up wherever shifts are claimed or assigned, so conflicts surface before they happen.
details: iOS: My Availability supports weekly blocks, one-time exceptions, preferred and avoid windows, and time off.
Anyone who works student shifts can manage availability, regardless of app role.
Open shifts and trades show time off, conflicts, and preferred windows; approved time off blocks claims.
iOS: Trade Board shows open shifts alongside posted trades, and Schedule filters live in one sheet.
Auto-fill explains why a slot stayed open, and subscribed calendar events show your area and call time.

title: Return Live Activity
summary: iPhone now shows a countdown on the lock screen and Dynamic Island as your checkout's return time approaches, so returns are harder to miss.
details: The countdown appears when your most urgent checkout is due within 30 minutes.
It ends automatically once the gear is returned at the kiosk.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Battery status, kiosk sleep mode, item edits, and several smaller issues were fixed this week.
details: Returned numbered batteries no longer show as checked out, and staff can repair stale battery records.
Kiosk: Overnight sleep mode follows local hours, and the scanner waits until you tap Start Scanning.
Department, location, and price edits save correctly on items and item families.
Settings appears in the web sidebar for everyone, and Bookings shows a badge when gear is due today.
iOS: Home loads faster with a lighter payload and cached thumbnails.
Guides have types like How-to, and Resources can switch between card and list views.

title: Smarter Items list
summary: Finding and managing gear is faster, with a popularity sort, smarter asset-tag handling, and an iPhone Items list that matches the web.
details: Sort by Most popular, based on how often items are checked out, reserved, and scanned.
Related asset tags sort together, and searching without dashes still finds tagged items.
Status badges show who has an item, and item families can be favorited and found by nickname.
iOS: Items and item families appear together with the same sorts and status colors as the web.
Deleting an item with booking history points you to Retire instead, and CSV export follows list filters.

title: Reserve gear that's due back in time
summary: Reservations can now include gear someone else has out, as long as it's due back before you need it.
details: Out gear can be reserved if it's due back at least an hour before your reservation starts.
Availability leaves a turnaround buffer between back-to-back bookings of the same item.
The equipment picker sorts by asset tag so copies of the same lens or body stay together.

title: Close a checkout without scanning
summary: Admins can close an open checkout from its detail page when all gear is verified back but can't be scanned.
details: Closing requires a reason and confirmation that the gear is back.
Closing marks items returned and puts batteries and stock back into availability.
The kiosk remains the standard place to return gear.

title: Live booking updates
summary: The dashboard, bookings list, booking details, and Items pages now refresh on their own when something changes, so staff always see current gear status.
details: An indicator shows whether sync is live, paused, offline, or retrying.
Checkout list and detail pages show whether booking changes are up to date.
Item lists and detail pages update when someone else changes an item.

title: Dedicated kiosk app
summary: The kiosk now runs as its own iPad app that opens straight into kiosk mode, so check-in stations no longer depend on the main app.
details: Kiosk lists and the hub load reliably instead of showing up empty.
When something fails, the kiosk shows the real reason instead of always blaming the internet.
Typing on the kiosk keeps the normal keyboard, and controls respond reliably.

title: Edit active checkouts at the kiosk
summary: Staff can change an active checkout at the kiosk without starting over or going to the web.
details: Change a checkout's title or return time.
Scan in another item to add it to the checkout.
Remove items that haven't been returned yet.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: All-day events display correctly everywhere, plus a round of kiosk, report, and item page fixes.
details: All-day events no longer show call times, midnight times, or an extra day on web, iPhone, and kiosk.
Items without a serial number open correctly again.
The camera preview on iPhone no longer shows a false error or jumps into Picture-in-Picture.
The Checkouts report no longer counts pending pickups or canceled bookings.
Kiosk Items Out and active checkouts now include numbered batteries, and battery-only returns count correctly.
iOS reservations group gear by category with photos and keep your pickup location.

title: Cleaner events and venue mapping
summary: Synced events get cleaner titles and more accurate home, away, and neutral labels, and each crew row shows one call time.
details: Event titles drop source prefixes, rankings, and school boilerplate, and venue spellings are cleaned up.
Each location's Home Venue setting decides whether a home-listed game is really home or neutral.
Admins can review venue mappings that are missing or point at inactive locations, with links to fix them.
Events can be marked Non-game, and the gear pickup location is set separately from the venue.
Crew rows, the assignment grid, and My Shifts show a single effective call time per person or slot.
Each person's Staff or Student scheduling class is set on their profile and drives labels and assignment.

title: Shift preferences and time off
summary: Students can tell staff when they prefer to work and request time off, so assignments account for more than class conflicts.
details: Students mark times they prefer or dislike working.
Time-off requests go to staff, who approve or deny them.

title: Smarter staffing tools
summary: Staff get ranked suggestions, an auto-fill preview, and work queues that point to exactly what still needs attention before an event.
details: The assign picker ranks people as Recommended, Good fit, Warning, or Overloaded, with short reasons.
Auto-fill previews proposed assignments, skipped slots, and warnings before anything changes.
Readiness cards and shareable work queues surface open slots, conflicts, pending requests, trades, and gear gaps.
Event pages compare a crew to the sport template and preview copying crew from the last matching event.
Schedule flags events missing a sport, opponent, or venue, and exports rosters, hours, and conflicts to CSV.
Events and assignments show whether gear is reserved, ready for pickup, or checked out.

title: Draft crews and publishing
summary: Crews can be built as drafts and published when ready, so workers only hear about changes once the schedule is final.
details: Staff publish a crew when it's ready, and assigned workers can acknowledge their shifts.
Draft changes don't notify anyone until published, and schedule and trade alerts open the related event.
Published open Student slots appear on the Trade Board alongside posted trades.
Event pages list recent crew, shift, publish, and gear changes, flagging ones made after publishing.
Notification settings add toggles for schedule, trade, and gear-prep alerts.

title: Reservation pickup at the kiosk
summary: Reservations that are due now show up on the kiosk as pickups, and scanning the gear turns the reservation into a checkout.
details: Due reservations appear on the kiosk; scan the gear and confirm to start the checkout.
A pickup that was started and left can be resumed with earlier scans already checked off.
Rows in Items Out, Active Checkouts, and Overdue open a detail view of who has the gear and when it's due.
A status dot shows connection health, with a Retry banner when a refresh fails.
If someone takes an item at the same moment, checkout shows a clear conflict message.

title: Kiosk checkout with Wiscard
summary: Students start at the kiosk by scanning their Wiscard, and every kiosk checkout now records what the gear is for and when it's coming back.
details: Scanning a Wiscard opens that person's kiosk hub, with the roster and a new A to Z filter as a fallback.
Checkouts ask for an upcoming event or a purpose, which becomes the booking title.
A return time picker checks scanned gear against other bookings and tight turnarounds before finishing.
Scanned gear shows photos, and numbered batteries, including older label formats, group into one row with unit chips.
Kiosk scans update each item's location and note when gear wasn't where expected.
Profiles hold a Wiscard number, admins can reset a kiosk's activation code, and staff can test hand scanners on iOS.

title: Checkouts move to the kiosk
summary: Gear now changes hands only at the kiosk. The web and iOS apps create reservations and show checkouts and their history.
details: Starting a checkout, picking up a reservation, and returning gear happen at the kiosk only.
Item pages offer Reserve instead of Check out.
Missing-gear actions on an event reserve gear for the assigned worker instead of starting a checkout.
Event pages label crew gear, reservations, and missing gear consistently, and prompt you to set up a crew first.

title: Kiosk visual consistency
summary: Colors, buttons, and progress rings now match across every kiosk screen, with larger touch targets.
details: Progress rings run blue to green on every screen, and completion buttons use Wisconsin red.
Overdue is red everywhere, and pickups waiting on you are orange.
Back, camera, and remove-item buttons are large enough to tap easily.

title: iOS Schedule with multi-day events
summary: The iOS Schedule adopts the new card style and shows events that span several days.
details: Multi-day events appear on every day they cover with a Day n of m marker.
Event detail and date headers have a cleaner design.

title: iOS Liquid Glass redesign
summary: The iOS app moves to a shared card style with native Liquid Glass controls across its main screens.
details: Home, Bookings, Items, and detail screens share one card style.
Forms, Schedule, and Login adopt Liquid Glass controls.
Booking detail, the bookings list, and Home show real user photos.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Kiosk activation and pickup problems are fixed, along with several iPhone loading issues.
details: Reopening the kiosk app, updates, and brief network drops no longer send the kiosk back to activation.
Scanning items at kiosk pickup no longer fails, and server errors show a plain try-again message.
Fixed a crash when opening Schedule on iPhone.
Creating bookings, deleting shifts, crew setup, trade cancel, and notification settings work correctly on iPhone again.
Quick search opens only from its button or Cmd/Ctrl+K, so typing in page fields isn't interrupted.
Settings no longer shows an active kiosk as offline, and dashboard View all links respect filters.

title: Kiosk standby clock
summary: The kiosk stays awake as an always-on station, showing a live clock and today's events between sessions.
details: The kiosk stays signed in, its screen no longer sleeps, and the home screen shows a large live clock.
At night or when idle, it dims to a moving clock to protect the screen, and a tap wakes it.
Home lists today's and tomorrow's events with assigned crew, and tapping one shows event and call times.
Items Out, Active Checkouts, and Overdue stat cards open their matching lists with item photos.
Activation accepts a hardware keyboard and paste, and says when a code is too short or invalid.

title: Battery label export
summary: Staff can print numbered battery labels in bulk and keep track of which units already have one.
details: Export battery labels as a CSV for the label printer.
Mark which unit labels have been printed.

title: Scan result card on iOS
summary: Scanning a single item on iOS opens a rich card, so you can see who has it and reserve it in one step.
details: The card shows the item's photo, status, availability, current holder, and due date.
Buttons reserve the item or open its full page.
Numbered battery labels now resolve to the right battery family when scanned or searched.

title: Camera firmware tracking
summary: Camera pages show whether firmware is current, and admins hear about new releases without checking manually.
details: Camera pages show installed and latest firmware with a color badge.
Admins get a notification when a newer firmware version is released for watched gear.

title: iOS Settings hub
summary: The iPhone Profile tab becomes a full Settings hub, bringing notification and account controls to parity with the web.
details: Settings groups account, schedule, notifications, appearance, and tools.
Notifications holds permission recovery, pause, channels, and the same category toggles as the web.
Account & Security lets you change your password and sign out other devices.
Tapping a shift notification opens Schedule to that event.

title: Faster item entry and shorter QR codes
summary: Adding gear takes fewer required fields, and new QR codes are shorter and easier to read on labels.
details: Only asset tag, category, location, and QR code are required; other details can be filled in later.
Add item suggests the next asset tag in a family as you type and can save a photo right after creation.
New QR codes are eight characters long, and existing labels keep working.
The QR dialog downloads a PNG for printing and confirms before replacing a code.
Item detail has grouped sections, an Attachments tab, and Reserve buttons that explain what's blocking them.

title: Refreshed booking creation
summary: Creating a reservation or checkout is calmer and more direct on both web and iPhone, with events filling in the details for you.
details: Creation leads with the event or booking title, with simpler field groups and compact selected-gear chips.
iOS reservations support scan-to-add, battery quantities, and a Confirm step before reserving.
On iPhone, link up to three upcoming events and the title, location, and times fill in automatically.
The requester picker shows photos with you pinned first, and changing the start time keeps the booking length.
iOS booking rows show live pickup and due countdowns plus a kiosk next-step banner.

title: Invitation-only onboarding
summary: New accounts are created by invitation only, so every person sets their own password when they sign up.
details: One Onboard users dialog handles single and bulk invites, flagging duplicates and existing accounts before sending.
An onboarding status page shows pending, stale, and claimed invitations.
Staff can copy a sign-up link for an unclaimed invitation or remove a stale one.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Booking forms, lists, and sync tools recover better from errors, and report exports are complete.
details: Checkout and reservation forms offer a retry when events or kits fail to load.
Canceled checkouts and reservations leave the active list right away, and older history offers a retry.
Resources search matches text inside guides again.
Every report export includes all matching rows, and Utilization and Missing Units gain CSV export.
Scanning the same item twice at kiosk pickup now says it was already scanned.
The audit log keeps your place when loading fails, and escalation and export saves are more reliable.

title: Clearer iOS labels and error recovery
summary: The iOS app trades icon-only controls for clear labels and recovers gracefully when something fails or a list is empty.
details: Buttons and tabs use visible labels like Claim shift, Assign person, Create Reservation, and My Gear.
Empty and failed lists offer Clear search, Show all, New Reservation, or Retry.

Choose a kit when creating a booking and see it labeled on the booking.

title: Bookings page and sidebar
summary: Checkouts and reservations now share one Bookings page, and the sidebar surfaces what needs attention.
details: Bookings lists both types with a card view, overdue bookings first.
New bookings open in a side panel without leaving the page.
The equipment picker searches across all sections with keyboard navigation and photo thumbnails.
The sidebar collapses and shows counts for overdue gear and unread notifications.
The dashboard shows recent activity as a chart and remembers saved filter views.

title: One Schedule page
summary: Events and shifts now live together on a single Schedule page, so crew coverage is visible right next to each event.
details: List and calendar views with coverage badges and full sport names.
A My Shifts filter, and events expand to show who is working each area.
Staff can add or remove shifts per event and assign anyone from an avatar picker.
Manual shift edits are kept when the calendar syncs.

title: Unified booking detail page
summary: Checkouts and reservations share one detail page with clearer status, actions, and progress.
details: Activity history reads in plain language.
Edit a booking's title inline.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Interface refresh, sign-in, and iPhone fixes.
details: Menus, dialogs, tables, and buttons share a consistent new look.
Sign-in adds show password, stay signed in, and password recovery.
Settings uses tab navigation, and Calendar Sources shows sync status and errors.
Events are grouped by day, and calendar days expand to show everything scheduled.
Reports add date filters, CSV export, and utilization charts.
Buttons guard against double-submits, and pages warn before you leave with unsaved changes.

title: Rebuilt Items list
summary: The Items list is rebuilt for speed, with broader search and better tools for working with many items.
details: Search covers tags, brand, model, serial, notes, category, location, and department.
Sort, filter by department, choose columns, and act on rows from a menu.
Create items in a side panel with QR codes you can generate or scan.
Select several items for bulk actions, and use a card view on phones.

title: Item and profile photos
summary: Items and people can now have photos, which makes the right gear and the right person easier to spot.
details: Add an item photo by uploading a file or pasting a link.
Profile photos appear on the dashboard and sidebar.

title: Event command center
summary: Each event gets one page showing its crew, who has gear, and who is still missing gear.
details: Staff can nudge crew members who haven't picked up gear.
Gear booked for an event links to the person's shift, so the page shows each crew member's gear status.
Creating a checkout for an event shows your shift area and time for that event.

title: Users directory redesign
summary: The Users directory gets real search and filters, and each person gets a profile page.
details: Profile pages have Info and Activity tabs with phone, primary area, and sport rosters.
Mobile-friendly cards replace the table on phones.

title: Due-date reminders
summary: Checkouts now send in-app and email reminders before gear is due, when it is due, and when it is overdue.
details: Overdue reminders also go out by email.
A reports hub shows who tends to return gear late.

title: Shift scheduling and Trade Board
summary: Every synced event now gets shifts. Staff assign crew by area, students pick up open slots, and the Trade Board handles swaps.
details: Admins set how many people each area needs for home and away games per sport.
Post a shift you can't work, and a teammate can claim it with staff approval.
Getting a shift sends a gear-up reminder, and My Shifts on the dashboard shows gear status.
Email notifications when you're assigned to or removed from a shift.
Scheduling guards against overlapping assignments.

title: Reference numbers, drafts, and accessories
summary: Bookings get short reference numbers and saved drafts, and accessories can travel with their main item.
details: Every booking gets a short, searchable reference number shown in lists and details.
Unfinished bookings are saved as drafts you can resume or discard from the dashboard.
Accessories link to a parent item and are grouped under it in the Items list.

title: Bulk inventory
summary: Pooled gear like batteries and cables can be tracked by quantity, or by numbered unit so missing pieces can be traced.
details: Create items as individually tracked gear or as bulk stock.
Give each bulk unit its own number, like battery #7, to spot losses.

title: Usage reports
summary: Report pages show how gear is used and where it goes, with charts, filters, and date ranges.
details: Covers utilization, checkout activity, overdue gear, missing units, scans, and audit history.
Reports are organized into tabs, with metric cards above the charts.
Each report shows a clear empty state or error when there's nothing to load.

title: Spreadsheet import with column mapping
summary: Importing gear from a CSV is more reliable for large files and shows exactly what will happen first.
details: Match spreadsheet columns to item fields.
Preview which rows will be created, updated, or skipped before importing.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Picker, user management, and calendar improvements.
details: Equipment picker adds multi-select, per-section search, availability badges, and scan-to-add.
Staff can search users and edit roles and locations inline, with changes recorded.
Events show sport and venue and can be viewed on a calendar.
Admins can turn calendar sources on or off and tune overdue reminders.
Students can view all bookings, with edit access limited to their own.

title: Scan modes
summary: The scan page can look up an item, add gear to a checkout, or check gear back in.
details: Lookup mode shows an item's status, holder, and location in a sheet without leaving the scan page.
Checkout and check-in scans track progress item by item and celebrate when everything is scanned.
Students can scan their own gear out and back in without staff help.

title: iPhone-friendly web app
summary: Pages are reworked for phone screens, and the web app can be installed on your home screen.
details: Larger tap targets across the app.
Students get a simpler sidebar, can scan their own gear, and see it highlighted in My Gear.
Dark mode follows your device setting or can be set by hand.
Search across the app from anywhere with a keyboard shortcut.

title: Operations dashboard
summary: The dashboard shows what is out and what is due, split into your gear and team activity.
details: Countdowns change color as due times approach.
Overdue items are called out in a banner at the top.
A stat strip and upcoming events round out the view.

title: Reservations and pickup
summary: Gear can be reserved ahead of time and turned into a checkout at pickup.
details: Duplicate an existing reservation to start a new one with the same gear.
Search, filter, and sort checkouts and reservations.

title: Items list and detail pages
summary: Browse all gear with filters, then open any item to see its bookings, info, and full history.
details: Staff can edit item details inline.
Organize gear into categories.
The History tab shows everything that has happened to an item.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Early reliability fixes for calendar sync and error handling.
details: One bad calendar entry no longer stops other events from syncing.
Unexpected errors show a recovery screen instead of a blank page.

title: Checkout workflow
summary: Checkouts get a real workflow: pick gear by section, return it in parts, and see conflicts before they happen.
details: An equipment picker groups gear by section, with kits shown first.
Return some items now and the rest later.
Warnings show when an item is already booked or a piece like a battery is missing.
Open any booking to change its gear, extend it, or cancel it.
Checkouts link to events and can be filtered by sport.

title: Wisconsin Creative, first build
summary: The first working build lays the foundation: an equipment inventory, synced athletics calendars, QR labels, and accounts. It is early groundwork, not yet in daily use.
details: Track each item's location, status, and who has it.
Game and event calendars sync into the app.
Scan gear with a phone camera and print QR labels.
Import existing gear from a spreadsheet with a preview first.
Account registration, profiles, and a notification center.
